decisions.reason: A safety shoe line is core to the firm's main business and involves substantial development and tooling investment, so dropping it after one year would write off sunk costs and contradict its innovation narrative.

The comfort insole is only mentioned on the website and is a low-investment accessory, which makes it more expendable, but insoles complement the shoe range and one year of results is too early to rule out temporary causes.

The supportive insole is a modest, low-visibility accessory that could be consolidated with other insoles, but it supports the firm's tailored-fit positioning and there is little reason yet to abandon it.

The ergonomic series has a dedicated page signalling visible public commitment and heavy investment, and it is central to the announced direction of developing tomorrow's footwear innovations, so management will persist with it.

Firefighter boots require costly certification and specialised development, so the sunk costs and entry into a new segment make withdrawal unlikely while early results can still be attributed to ramp-up.
Featuring the moulded insole on the home page is a highly visible commitment, so dropping it would publicly expose the decision as a mistake, and management will likely keep it.
